I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My two boys moved to the city years ago — one is in Shijiazhuang, the other in Beijing. It is just me and my wife now. We are not young anymore. My back gives me trouble. We manage together, and during the busy seasons my youngest son sometimes comes back to help with the machines.

This land is about 5 mu. That is what we can handle at our age. More would kill us.

The question is not really "what to grow." It has never been a question. We grow wheat in the winter and corn in the summer. That is what everyone around here does. That is what my father did. The soil knows it, the market knows it, and I know it. Why would I change at 73?

For the wheat, I will put in Jimai seed — the improved kind the cooperative sells. I have used it for several years now and the yields are decent. I put down fertilizer before sowing and again at jointing. Water three times: once before sowing to wet the ground good, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling out. I spray twice — once for weeds early on and once later for aphids and rust if I see it. I use the rotary tiller to turn the soil in autumn before planting. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn on the same ground. No plowing — I just direct seed into the stubble. The hybrid seed from Zhengdan or whatever the cooperative has that year. Corn needs less babying than wheat in my experience. Water twice — once around knee-high and once when it tassels. Fertilizer goes in at planting and then a top dressing when it is shooting up. Spray twice. By October it is done.

That is the whole year. Same as last year. Same as the year before.
